correctness.rationale: Identical a_ij=1/4 midpoint rows with equal initial stage guesses yield exact scalar Picard F_x(y)=x/[1+s(1+b y^2)^(m/2)] and unique implicit positive root. The logarithmic slope q_m(y)=m*(b y^2/(1+b y^2))*(s(1+b y^2)^(m/2)/(1+s(1+b y^2)^(m/2))) increases strictly to m. On (0,x] q_m(x)<1 for 0<m<=1, establishing true contraction in log coordinates. For m>1 the unique q_m(y_c)=1 gives a repelling fixed point when x>x_c; F_x is decreasing on [0,x], hence F_x^2 increasing and initial upper/lower subsequences monotone. Repelling r excludes coincident limits, proving real nonvanishing two-cycle. For m=2 the two-cycle equations imply yz=A/B and x=A(y+z), giving the exact pair and multiplier 4A^3/(Bx^2). Boundary x=x_c has no distinct period-two roots and converges. 50 independent bounded numerical tests agree, not a universal proof.
residual_risks: Unconditional global convergence concerns iterations from y0=x and 0<m<=1 at finite x; the contraction constant tends to 1 in stiff limits.
